full_judgment:
Mr. A.B. M. Khairul Haque, J: This rule under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure was issued at the instance of Md. Nurul Hoque and others calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-3, to show cause as to why the order dated 20.03.1991 passed by the senior Assistant Judge, Cox;s Bazar , in Miscellaneous case No. 32 of 1990, should not be set aside. 

 2. The petitioners filed a suit being Title Suit No. 112 of 1986 in the court of senior Assistant Judge, Cox's Bazar, praying for declaration of their title in the suit land. But the suit was dismissed on 20.05.1990 for default. Thereafter the petitioner filed an application under Order IX rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, praying for restoration of the suit and a miscellaneous case being Miscellaneous Case No. 32 of 1990 was started on 29.05.1990. This case was also dismissed for not taking steps on 13.03.1991 as directed by the learned court on 05.03.1991. Thereafter on 20.03.1991 the plaintiff filed an application under section 151 of the Code praying for vacating the order of dismissal of the case passed on 13.03.1991 and for restoring the miscellaneous case to its original file and number. The said petition was rejected by the learned Senior Assistant Judge by his order dated 20.03.1991. Being aggrieved the petitioner obtained the present rule. 

 Besides, be submits that due to unavoidable reason the learned Advocate could not appear on the date fixed to take necessary steps but discovered subsequently that the miscellaneous case had already been dismissed for not talking steps. The learned Advocate on behalf of the petitioner immediately filed an application on 20.03.1991 after complying the direction of the court. As such, she submits that rejection of the petition under section 15I of the Code of Civil Procedure was illegal and is liable to be set aside. 

 5. Heard the learned Advocate and perused the petition. It appears that after dismissal of the suit the petitioner filed a miscellaneous case under Order IX rule 9 of the Code for restoration of their suit and along with their miscellaneous case, filed necessary summons and notices and other requisites. On the orders of the Court the petitioners also filed the requisites on further three occasions. It appears that 05.03.1991 was fixed for returns after service of summons upon the opposite parties. On that date the petitioners were not present, as such, could not know the order passed on 05.03.1991, directing them to file the requisites all over again on 13.03.1991. It also appears that they are also absent on 13.03.1992 and could not take any steps for filing the requisites in Court for service upon the opposite parties. As such, the miscellaneous case was dismissed on that for default. 

 Code explained that due to the illness of his mother, the clerk of the learned Advocate left for his home as such could not inform the learned Advocate of the petitioners about the steps to be taken on 13.03.1991 and consequently the learned Advocate failed to take steps on that date. It appears also that on 20.03.1991 the necessary requisites had already been submitted in court. It appears that the case was dismissed for not taking necessary steps in filing the requisites, as such, an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, praying for restoration of the miscellaneous case is maintainable. Besides the opposite parties also did not appear at that time, 

 9. In the result, this rule is made absolute and the miscellaneous case filed under Order IX 

 10. Since the case is an old one of 1990 the learned Senior Assistant Judge is directed dispose of the miscellaneous case expeditiously following the procedure laid down in rule 125
